To merge the last two commits in Git, you can use an interactive rebase. Here are the main methods:

## Method 1: Interactive Rebase (Recommended)

```bash
git rebase -i HEAD~2
```

This opens your text editor with something like:
```
pick abc1234 Second to last commit
pick def5678 Last commit
```

Change `pick` to `squash` (or `s`) on the second line:
```
pick abc1234 Second to last commit
squash def5678 Last commit
```

Save and close the editor. Git will then prompt you to edit the commit message for the combined commit.

## Method 2: Soft Reset

```bash
git reset --soft HEAD~2
git commit -m "New combined commit message"
```

This undoes the last 2 commits but keeps all changes staged, then creates a new single commit.

## Method 3: Amend (if merging into the previous commit)

```bash
git reset --soft HEAD~1
git commit --amend
```

This undoes the last commit and amends it to the previous one.

## Important Notes

⚠️ **Warning**: Only do this if you haven't pushed these commits to a shared repository. If you've already pushed, you'll need to force push (`git push --force`) which can cause problems for other developers.

If you've already pushed and others might have pulled, it's better to leave the history as-is to avoid conflicts.
